BookStore REST API (1.0.0)

Download OpenAPI specification:

License: Apache 2.0

REST API for an online bookstore.

This API provides authentication, user management, book management, cart, favourites, orders, and other bookstore-related functionality.

auth

Authentication and account verification endpoints.

Includes:

  • User registration
  • User login
  • Email OTP verification
  • Resending OTP
  • Forgot password
  • Reset password

Register a new user account

Creates a new customer account in the BookStore database using the supplied personal details, contact numbers, date of birth, and physical delivery address.

Upon account creation:

  1. A user record is persisted in MongoDB with role: "user", isEmailVerified: false, isActive: true, and an empty cart and favourites list.
  2. A 6-digit numeric verification OTP is generated with a 30-second expiration window (verificationTokenExpiry).
  3. An HTML verification email is dispatched via Nodemailer to the user's email address (or development mailbox).
  4. If the email fails to deliver, the newly created user record is rolled back and deleted from the database.
  5. The client must submit the received OTP to /auth/verifyOtp within 30 seconds to verify their email and obtain an access token.

Rate limit: 5 requests per minute.

Request Body schema: application/json
required

Personal and delivery details required to register a customer account.

name
required
string >= 2 characters

The user's full name.

email
required
string <email>

Email address used for the user's account.

password
required
string <password> >= 8 characters

Password used to authenticate the user.

dateOfBirth
required
string <date>

The user's date of birth.

phoneNumber
required
integer

The user's 10-digit phone number.

gender
required
string
Enum: "male" "female" "others"

Gender selected by the user.

required
object (Address)

Physical address associated with a user.

Responses

Authenticate user and receive JWT access token

Authenticates an existing user account using email and password credentials.

Authentication flow:

  1. Express-validator checks that email and password fields are present and well-formed.
  2. User is looked up in MongoDB by email address.
  3. check if user account is verified, if it is then return error message
  4. The submitted plain password is verified against the bcrypt password hash.
  5. A JSON Web Token (JWT) signed with JWT_SECRET_KEY and configured expiration (JWT_EXPIRES) is generated containing the user ID payload { id: userId }.
  6. The JWT token and complete user profile are returned to the client.

Client requests to protected endpoints must supply this token in the header: Authorization: Bearer <JWT_TOKEN>

Rate limit: 5 requests per minute.

Request Body schema: application/json
required

User credentials for login authentication.

email
required
string <email>

Email address associated with the user account.

password
required
string <password>

Password associated with the user account.

Responses

Verify email verification OTP

Verifies the 6-digit one-time password (OTP) sent to the user's email during registration.

Verification logic:

  1. Client provides email and the 6-digit otp.
  2. Server checks if the user account exists in MongoDB.
  3. Verifies whether the account is already verified (isEmailVerified === true).
  4. Checks whether the OTP has expired (Date.now() > verificationTokenExpiry).
  5. Validates the submitted OTP against the stored emailVerifiedToken.
  6. Upon successful verification:
    • isEmailVerified is updated to true.
    • emailVerifiedToken and verificationTokenExpiry are cleared.
    • A signed JWT access token is minted and returned so the user can immediately interact with protected endpoints.

Rate limit: 5 requests per minute.

Request Body schema: application/json
required

Email address and 6-digit verification OTP.

otp
required
integer [ 100000 .. 999999 ]

Six-digit OTP sent to the user's email.

email
required
string <email>

Email address associated with the account.

Responses

Resend email verification OTP

Generates and sends a new 6-digit verification OTP to the user's registered email address.

Endpoint rules:

  1. The account must exist in the database.
  2. If the user's email is already verified (isEmailVerified === true), resending is rejected with 400.
  3. A fresh OTP is generated with a new 30-second expiry timestamp.
  4. An HTML email with the new OTP is dispatched via Nodemailer.

Rate limit: 5 requests per minute.

Request Body schema: application/json
required

Email address of the unverified customer account.

email
required
string <email>

Email address associated with the user account.

Responses

Request password reset email link

Generates a secure password reset token and emails a reset link to the user.

Security & controller requirements:

  1. Protected Route: Requires a valid JWT Bearer token in the Authorization header (protect middleware).
  2. The authenticated user must have a verified email address (isEmailVerified === true).
  3. The email to reset is provided in the request body.
  4. A 32-byte cryptographically secure random token is generated and SHA-256 hashed into passwordResetToken on the user record.
  5. The reset token has a 30-second expiry (passwordExpires = Date.now() + 30 * 1000).
  6. An email containing the password reset link ${protocol}://${host}/auth/resetPassword/${resetToken} is sent to the customer.

Rate limit: 5 requests per minute.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
Request Body schema: application/json
required

Email address of the account requesting password reset.

email
required
string <email>

Email address associated with the account.

Responses

Reset user password using reset token

Changes the user's password using the unhashed password reset token received via email.

Flow & controller requirements:

  1. Protected Route: Requires a valid JWT Bearer token in the Authorization header (protect middleware).
  2. The reset token is supplied as a URL path parameter :token.
  3. The server hashes :token with SHA-256 and searches for a user where passwordResetToken matches and passwordExpires > Date.now().
  4. If the token is invalid or expired (30-second lifespan), an error is returned.
  5. The new password is set, passwordResetToken and passwordExpires are cleared to undefined, and the user document is saved (which triggers bcrypt hashing via Mongoose pre('save')).

Rate limit: 5 requests per minute.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
path Parameters
token
required
string
Example: a1b2c3d4e5f67890123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0

Unhashed password reset token string extracted from the email link.

Request Body schema: application/json
required

The new password to replace the current password.

password
required
string <password> >= 8 characters

New password that replaces the existing password.

Responses

Local Development Server

http://bookstore.kplabs.com/api/auth/resetpassword/{token}

admin

Administrator endpoints for monitoring and managing the bookstore application.

Get admin dashboard statistics

Retrieves aggregated key performance statistics for the administrator dashboard.

The dashboard aggregates:

  • Total revenue from non-cancelled orders
  • Total count of orders (all statuses)
  • Total books Ordered in system
  • Total sales and order count for the current month
  • Total sales and order count for the current year
  • Daily paid sales for the last 30 days
  • Best-selling book (by units sold and revenue)
  • Total registered users count
  • New users registered during the current month
  • User distribution by non-admin roles (user, seller, etc.)
  • Orders grouped by order status (paid, pending, cancelled, etc.)
  • Pending orders count
  • Books with low inventory (stock <= 10)

Rate limit: 30 requests per minute.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth

Responses

Get sales and revenue analytics

Retrieves aggregated sales metrics for non-cancelled orders grouped by day, week, or month.

Optional query parameters allow filtering by date range (startDate and endDate) and selecting the aggregation period (groupBy):

  • day: Groups data daily (YYYY-MM-DD) [default]
  • week: Groups data weekly (YYYY-Www)
  • month: Groups data monthly (YYYY-MM)

For each time bucket, the response returns:

  • totalRevenue: Sum of total prices
  • avgRevenue: Average order value
  • totalOrders: Count of orders
  • totalItems: Total quantity of books purchased

Rate limit: 30 requests per minute.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
query Parameters
startDate
string <date>
Example: startDate=2026-01-01

Earliest order creation date to include (inclusive).

endDate
string <date>
Example: endDate=2026-10-01

Latest order creation date to include (inclusive).

groupBy
string
Default: "day"
Enum: "day" "week" "month"
Example: groupBy=day

Time-series bucket granularity.

Responses

http://bookstore.kplabs.com/api/admin/getSalesAnalytics

Get books with zero sales in the last 30 days

Identifies stagnant inventory ("dead stock") books that have generated zero sales in paid orders over the past 30 days.

Returns paginated book items with title, author, current stock, price, and totalSold: 0.

Get month-by-month sales trends per category

Computes monthly sales quantities and revenue per category within a specified date range.

Validations enforced:

  • startDate and endDate are required valid date strings.
  • endDate must be strictly after startDate.
  • The date range between startDate and endDate cannot exceed 1 year.

Missing calendar months in the range are automatically densified with zero values.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
query Parameters
startDate
required
string <date>
Example: startDate=2026-01-01

Start date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

endDate
required
string <date>
Example: endDate=2026-09-01

End date in YYYY-MM-DD format (must be within 1 year from startDate).

books

Book catalog, inventory, and product management endpoints.

Includes:

  • Public catalog browsing with title and author regex search
  • Sorting (newest, oldest) and pagination controls
  • Single book lookup with high-speed Redis caching
  • Administrator book creation with Cloudinary cover image upload
  • Administrator book updates with metadata editing and cover image replacement
  • Administrator soft-deletion preserving historical order data

Retrieve all books with search, sort, and pagination

Retrieves a paginated collection of active books from the catalog.

Supports keyword filtering by book title and author using case-insensitive regular expressions ($regex, $options: "i"). Results can be sorted in descending (newest) or ascending (oldest) chronological order by creation date.

Soft Deletion & Visibility

Soft-deleted books (isDeleted: true) are automatically excluded from the result set by a Mongoose pre(/^find/) query middleware.

Search & Filtering Capabilities

  • Title Search: Substring match against book titles.
  • Author Search: Substring match against author names.
  • Both filters can be used independently or combined.

Sorting Behavior

  • sort=new (default): Sorts descending by -createdAt (newest books first).
  • sort=old: Sorts ascending by createdAt (oldest books first).
  • Any unrecognized sort parameter defaults to new.

Pagination Rules

  • page: 1-based page index (defaults to 1).
  • limit: Number of records returned per page (defaults to 10).
  • Upper Bound: If limit exceeds 100, the server automatically caps it at 100.
  • Computes skip = (page - 1) * limit.
  • Computes totalPages = Math.ceil(totalItems / limit) and hasNextPage = page < totalPages.

Rate Limiting

  • Protected by getRateLimiter: Maximum 30 requests per minute per client IP.
query Parameters
title
string
Example: title=clean

Case-insensitive substring search for book title. Matches any book whose title contains the specified query text.

author
string
Example: author=martin

Case-insensitive substring search for author name. Matches any book written by an author matching the query string.

sort
string
Default: "new"
Enum: "new" "old"
Example: sort=new

Ordering criterion for the returned books:

  • new: Newest books first (sorted descending by creation date -createdAt).
  • old: Oldest books first (sorted ascending by creation date createdAt). Defaults to new if omitted or if an invalid option is provided.
page
integer >= 1
Default: 1
Example: page=1

1-based page number for paginated results.

limit
integer [ 1 .. 100 ]
Default: 10
Example: limit=10

Number of book records returned per page. Maximum allowed value is 100. Values exceeding 100 are automatically clamped to 100 by the server.

Create a new book with cover image upload

Creates and registers a new book entity in the bookstore catalog.

This operation is restricted to verified administrators (role: 'admin'). The request must be transmitted as multipart/form-data to accommodate both book metadata fields and the binary image file for the book's cover.

Creation & Upload Flow

  1. Authentication: Caller provides a valid JWT Bearer token in the Authorization header.
  2. Authorization: restrictTo("admin") middleware verifies the caller holds admin role and that their email is verified.
  3. Rate Limiting: mutationLimiter restricts the caller to 10 mutations per minute.
  4. File Handling: Multer parses the multipart request, extracting the file from field coverImage and writing it to temporary disk storage (uploads/).
  5. Validation: validateBooks validates the presence and constraints of title, author, stock, description, price, and category.
  6. Cloudinary Upload: The server uploads the temporary cover image to Cloudinary under the "BookStore" folder.
  7. Cleanup: The local temporary file is deleted from disk using fs.unlink.
  8. Database Persistence: A new document is saved in MongoDB with the resulting Cloudinary HTTPS URL and initial defaults (totalSales: 0, ratingAverage: 0, ratingQuantity: 0, isDeleted: false).
  9. Response: Returns HTTP 201 Created with the complete book document.

Validation Rules

  • title: String, trimmed, non-empty, minimum length of 2 characters.
  • author: String, non-empty.
  • stock: Numeric, non-empty, non-negative integer.
  • description: String, non-empty.
  • price: Numeric, non-empty, non-negative, minimum length 1 character.
  • category: Must match one of the predefined categories: Fantasy, Action, Adventure, Mystery, Horror, Thriller, Romance, Self-help, Biography. Cannot be empty.
  • coverImage: Required binary file representing the book cover art.
Authorizations:
bearerAuth

Multipart form data containing book metadata and the cover image file.

Title or name of the book (minimum 2 characters).

Initial inventory quantity. Must be a valid non-negative number.

required

Detailed description or synopsis of the book content.

required

Retail price of the book. Must be non-negative and at least 1 character in length.

category
required
string
Enum: "Fantasy" "Action" "Adventure" "Mystery" "Horror" "Thriller" "Romance" "Self-help" "Biography"

Genre category selected from the predefined list of allowed categories.

coverImage
required
string <binary>

Cover image file (JPEG, PNG, WebP) uploaded via form-data. The server automatically transmits this file to Cloudinary in the BookStore folder and deletes the local temporary file after upload.

Retrieve a book by its unique ID (with Redis caching)

Retrieves detailed information for a specific book identified by its unique MongoDB ObjectId.

High-Performance Redis Caching

This endpoint implements a cache-aside caching strategy using Redis:

  1. The server checks for the Redis key book:{bookId}.
  2. Cache Hit: If the key exists, cached JSON data is parsed and returned immediately without accessing the MongoDB database.
  3. Cache Miss:
    • Validates that bookId parameter is present and valid.
    • Queries MongoDB via Books.findById(bookId).
    • The Mongoose pre(/^find/) middleware automatically filters out soft-deleted books (isDeleted: false).
    • If the book is not found in MongoDB, returns HTTP 404 Not Found.
    • If found, writes the serialized book document into Redis under book:{bookId} and returns HTTP 200 OK.

Rate Limiting

  • Protected by getRateLimiter: Maximum 30 requests per minute per client IP.
path Parameters
bookId
required
string
Example: 683aab454ae6c56e60594eb7

24-character hexadecimal MongoDB ObjectId of the book to retrieve.

Update book details or replace cover image

Updates an existing book's metadata fields or replaces its cover image.

This operation is restricted to verified administrators (role: 'admin').

Update Workflow

  1. ID Validation: validateId("bookId") middleware verifies that bookId is a syntactically valid 24-character hexadecimal MongoDB ObjectId.
  2. Authentication & Authorization: protect and restrictTo("admin") ensure caller has active admin credentials.
  3. Rate Limiting: mutationLimiter enforces a rate limit of 10 requests per minute.
  4. Image Replacement (Optional): If a new coverImage file is attached via multipart/form-data:
    • The file is temporarily stored by Multer.
    • Uploaded to Cloudinary under the "BookStore" folder.
    • The local temporary file is removed via fs.unlink.
    • The new Cloudinary secure_url replaces the existing coverImage in the update payload.
  5. Database Update: Calls Books.findByIdAndUpdate(bookId, updatePayload).
  6. Cache Refresh: The updated book object is serialized and written to Redis key book:{bookId}, ensuring subsequent GET requests immediately reflect changes.
  7. Response: Returns HTTP 200 OK with the updated book entity.

Request Formats Supported

  • multipart/form-data: Use when replacing the cover image (with or without textual metadata changes).
  • application/json: Use when updating only text or numeric fields (title, author, price, stock, description, category).

Soft-delete a book from the catalog

Performs a soft deletion on the book specified by bookId.

This operation is restricted to verified administrators (role: 'admin').

Soft-Deletion Architecture

Rather than permanently purging the record from MongoDB, the controller updates the document with { isDeleted: true }:

  1. Preserves sales history, order relations, and aggregate analytics integrity.
  2. Mongoose pre(/^find/) middleware automatically intercepts all queries (find, findOne, findById) and applies { isDeleted: false }, ensuring deleted books are immediately hidden from the public store catalog.
  3. If the book does not exist or was already deleted, returns HTTP 404 Not Found.

Rate Limiting

  • Protected by generalRateLimiter: Maximum 15 requests per minute per client IP.
Authorizations:
bearerAuth

bookId
required
string
Example: 683aab454ae6c56e60594eb7

Shopping cart operations for authenticated customers.

Includes:

  • Retrieving active user shopping cart with Redis caching
  • Adding books to cart with real-time inventory validation and dynamic pricing recalculation
  • Removing items from cart with automatic price and quantity reconciliation

Retrieve the authenticated user's shopping cart

Retrieves the active shopping cart for the authenticated customer.

This endpoint requires authentication and is restricted to customers with role: 'user'. The user's email address must be verified.

High-Performance Redis Caching Architecture

The cart utilizes a cache-aside caching strategy via Redis:

  1. Cache Lookup: Checks Redis key user:{userId}:cart.
  2. Cache Hit:
    • If cached data is present, the server parses the JSON string and responds immediately with HTTP 200 OK without touching the MongoDB database: { status: "success", message: "cart is found", data: cartData }.
  3. Cache Miss:
    • Queries MongoDB for an existing cart via Cart.findOne({ user: userId }).
    • Writes the serialized result into Redis under key user:{userId}:cart.
    • If a cart exists in the database, returns HTTP 200 OK with { status: "success", data: getCart }.
    • If the user has not created or added any items to their cart yet, data is null.

Rate Limiting

  • Protected by getRateLimiter: Maximum 30 requests per minute per client IP.
Authorizations:
bearerAuth

Add a book to the shopping cart or increment quantity

Adds a specified quantity of a book to the authenticated customer's shopping cart.

If a cart does not yet exist for the user, a new one is initialized. If the item is already in the cart, its quantity is increased and financial totals are recalculated. Synchronizes changes with Redis caching.

This endpoint requires authentication and is restricted to customers with role: 'user'.

In-Depth Business & Controller Logic

  1. Input Extraction:
    • Extracts bookId and quantity from request body.
    • Extracts userId from authenticated req.user.id.
  2. Inventory Stock Pre-Check:
    • Queries Books.findById(bookId).
    • Verifies that book.stock >= quantity. If the requested quantity exceeds total book stock, rejects immediately with HTTP 400 Bad Request: "No book stock is available yet, please contact admin to futher information".
  3. Cart Discovery & Evaluation:
    • Queries MongoDB for an existing cart via Cart.findOne({ user: userId }).
  4. Branch A: Cart Does Not Exist:
    • Initializes a new Cart document:
      {
  "user": "userId",
  "items": [{ "book": "bookId", "quantity": quantity }],
  "totalQuantity": quantity,
  "totalPrice": book.price * quantity
}
  5. Branch B: Cart Already Exists:
    • Searches for bookId within cart.items:
      • Case 1: Book already exists in cart (index > -1):
        • Calculates newTotalQty = existingQty + quantity.
        • Stock Validation: If newTotalQty > book.stock, rejects with HTTP 400 Bad Request: "Only <availableStock> more units available".
        • Increments item quantity: cart.items[index].quantity += quantity.
        • Increments totals: cart.totalQuantity += quantity, cart.totalPrice += book.price * quantity.
      • Case 2: Book is new to this existing cart (index === -1):
        • Stock Validation: If quantity > book.stock, rejects with HTTP 400 Bad Request: "Only <availableStock> more units available".
        • Pushes new item to cart.items: { book: bookId, quantity }.
        • Increments totals: cart.totalQuantity += quantity, cart.totalPrice += book.price * quantity.
  6. Persistence & Cache Sync:
    • Persists cart to MongoDB: await cart.save().
    • Updates Redis cache key user:{userId}:cart with the newly saved cart JSON.
  7. Response:
    • Returns HTTP 200 OK with { status: "success", message: "added to cart", data: cart }.

Rate Limiting

  • Protected by mutationLimiter: Maximum 10 mutations per minute per client IP.

Remove a book from the shopping cart

Removes a specific book item entirely from the authenticated customer's shopping cart.

Automatically recalculates cumulative price (totalPrice) and quantity (totalQuantity) based on the removed book's unit price, and synchronizes the updated cart with Redis cache.

This endpoint requires authentication and is restricted to customers with role: 'user'.

In-Depth Business & Controller Logic

  1. Parameter & ObjectId Validation:
    • Middleware validateId("bookId") validates that bookId is a syntactically valid 24-character hexadecimal MongoDB ObjectId (mongoose.Types.ObjectId.isValid). If invalid, returns HTTP 400 Bad Request: "Invalid Id, please enter correct id".
    • If bookId is missing, returns HTTP 400 Bad Request: "please provide book id to remove a book from the cart".
  2. Cart Discovery:
    • Looks up the user's cart in MongoDB: Cart.findOne({ user: id }).
    • If no cart exists for the user, returns HTTP 404 Not Found: "cart not found, please create your cart first".
  3. Item Identification:
    • Searches for the book within cart.items: index = findExistingCart.items.findIndex(item => item.book.toString() === bookId).
    • If the book is not present in the cart (index === -1), returns HTTP 404 Not Found: "book not found in the cart".
  4. Price & Quantity Reconciliation:
    • Extracts the removed item's stored quantity: removedQty = removedItem.quantity.
    • Queries the book details from MongoDB (Books.findById(removedItem.book._id)) to get its unit price.
    • Computes deducted price: removedPrice = findBook.price * removedQty.
    • Splices the item out of the items array: cart.items.splice(index, 1).
    • Subtracts from totals:
      • cart.totalPrice -= removedPrice
      • cart.totalQuantity -= removedQty
    • Empty Cart Handling: If all items have been removed (cart.items.length === 0), explicitly resets totalPrice = 0 and totalQuantity = 0.
  5. Persistence & Cache Sync:
    • Saves the updated cart in MongoDB: await findExistingCart.save().
    • Updates Redis key user:{userId}:cart with the serialized updated cart.
  6. Response:
    • Returns HTTP 200 OK with { status: "success", message: "book was removed", data: findExistingCart }.

Rate Limiting

  • Protected by mutationLimiter: Maximum 10 mutations per minute per client IP.

bearerAuth

Example: 683aab454ae6c56e60594eb7

orders

Order processing, Stripe checkout, refund requests, and fulfillment tracking.

Includes:

  • Creating Stripe checkout sessions with inventory reservations and cart conversion
  • Processing customer payment refunds with eligibility verification (7-day window)
  • Administrator platform-wide order monitoring, sorting, and pagination

Create a Stripe checkout session for the authenticated user's cart

Initializes a secure, Stripe-hosted payment checkout session for all books currently stored in the authenticated customer's shopping cart.

Authentication & Access Control

  • Required Authentication: Bearer JWT token in the Authorization header (protect middleware).
  • Role Restriction: Strictly restricted to customers with role: 'user' (restrictTo("user")).
  • Email Verification: User account email address must be verified (isEmailVerified: true).

Complete Checkout & Inventory Lifecycle

  1. User & Cart Lookup: Retrieves the customer document and active cart via Cart.findOne({ user: req.user.id }) with populated book details (populate("items.book")). If no cart exists, returns HTTP 404 Not Found.
  2. Inventory Stock Validation & Reservation (makeReservation middleware):
    • Inspects every item in the cart against active inventory in the Books collection (Books.findById(item.book)).
    • If any requested quantity exceeds currently available inventory (book.stock < item.quantity), checkout halts immediately with HTTP 400 Bad Request ("We have only [stock] of [title] left").
    • Deletes any prior unfulfilled reservation for this user (Reservation.findByIdAndDelete).
    • Creates a new temporary reservation record in MongoDB (Reservation.create) to hold inventory while payment is processed.
  3. Stripe Checkout Session Creation:
    • Converts line items into Stripe line item format with currency: "inr", book title, unit amount (price converted to paise: unit_amount = book.price * 100), and quantity.
    • Calls stripe.checkout.sessions.create configured with mode: "payment" and payment_method_types: ["card"].
    • Dynamic redirect callback URLs:
      • success_url: {host}/orders/success?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}
      • cancel_url: {host}/orders/cancel
  4. Asynchronous Order Fulfillment via Queue (orderQueue):
    • Upon successful payment authorization, Stripe dispatches a checkout.session.completed webhook event.
    • The webhook handler enqueues an order-processing background job into BullMQ orderQueue.
    • A dedicated worker processes the session: generates the final Order record, marks the cart isOrdered: true, decrements book stock, updates sales metrics, and cleans up the reservation.

Rate Limiting

  • Protected by mutationLimiter: Maximum 10 mutation requests per minute per client IP.

Request a Stripe payment refund for an eligible paid order

Initiates a customer payment refund through the Stripe payment gateway for a completed order.

Authentication & Access Control

  • Required Authentication: Bearer JWT token (protect middleware).
  • Role Restriction: Strictly restricted to customers with role: 'user' (restrictTo("user")).
  • Email Verification: User account email address must be verified (isEmailVerified: true).

Eligibility Criteria & Validation Rules (checkRefundStatus middleware)

  1. Order Ownership Verification: Queries MongoDB for an order where paymentInfo.stripePaymentId matches the path parameter and user matches the authenticated customer (req.user._id). If no matching order is found, returns HTTP 404 Not Found ("Order not found").
  2. 7-Day Cancellation Window Enforcement: Refunds are strictly permitted within 168 hours (7 calendar days) of order payment (paidAt). If todayDate > (paidAt + 168 hours), the request is rejected with HTTP 400 Bad Request ("date is passed, you can't make a refund request").
  3. Order Status Requirement: The order must be in "paid" status. Unpaid, pending, or already cancelled orders cannot be refunded ("This payment cannot be refunded").

Refund Execution & Catalog Reconciliation

  • Invokes stripe.refunds.create({ payment_intent: stripePaymentId, reason: "requested_by_customer" }).
  • Automated Webhook Synchronization (charge.refunded): Upon Stripe refund confirmation, the incoming webhook handler:
    • Updates order status: orderStatus = "cancelled", paymentInfo.status = "cancelled".
    • Executes Mongoose bulkWrite to replenish catalog stock (stock += quantity) and decrement revenue figures (totalSales -= salesAmount) on affected Books documents.

Rate Limiting

  • Protected by rate limiting: Maximum 30 requests per minute per client IP.

Retrieve all platform orders with sorting and pagination (Admin only)

Retrieves a paginated list of all customer orders across the platform for administrative auditing, status tracking, and fulfillment operations.

Authentication & Access Control

  • Required Authentication: Bearer JWT token (protect middleware).
  • Role Restriction: Strictly restricted to users holding role: 'admin' (restrictTo("admin")).
  • Email Verification: Admin account email address must be verified (isEmailVerified: true).

Sorting Behavior

  • sort=new (default): Sorts descending by -createdAt (most recent orders first).
  • sort=old: Sorts ascending by createdAt (oldest orders first).
  • Unrecognized or omitted sort parameter automatically defaults to new.

Pagination Rules

  • page: 1-based page index (defaults to 1).
  • limit: Number of records returned per page (defaults to 10).
  • Upper Bound: If limit exceeds 100, the server automatically caps it at 100.
  • Computes skip = (page - 1) * limit.
  • Computes totalPages = Math.ceil(totalItems / limit) and hasNextPage = page < totalPages.
  • Dynamic response message: "all orders found successfully" when records match, or "orders not found" when the catalog yields 0 records.

Rate Limiting

  • Protected by getRateLimiter: Maximum 30 requests per minute per client IP.

Retrieve an order by unique ID (with Redis caching)

Retrieves the complete document details of an individual order by its unique identifier, utilizing a high-performance Redis cache-aside caching pattern.

Authentication & Access Control

  • Required Authentication: Bearer JWT token (protect middleware).
  • Role Restriction: Accessible to customers and administrators (role: 'user' or 'admin').
  • Email Verification: User account email address must be verified (isEmailVerified: true).
  • Parameter Validation: Middleware validateId("orderId") verifies that orderId is a syntactically valid 24-character hexadecimal MongoDB ObjectId before controller execution.

High-Performance Redis Cache-Aside Architecture

  1. Cache Lookup: Queries Redis in-memory cache for key order:{orderId} using client.get(...).
  2. Cache Hit:
    • Returns cached serialized order JSON immediately from memory without querying MongoDB.
    • Responds with HTTP 200 OK: { status: "success", data: JSON.parse(orderData) }.
  3. Cache Miss:
    • Queries MongoDB via Order.findById(orderId).
    • If no order exists, aborts with HTTP 404 Not Found ("Order not found").
    • If found:
      • Serializes the order document and stores it in Redis under key order:{orderId}.
      • Responds with HTTP 200 OK: { status: "success", data: order }.

Rate Limiting

  • Protected by getRateLimiter: Maximum 30 requests per minute per client IP.

Submit a new customer review and rating for a book

Creates a new review commentary and numerical star rating for the designated book.

Authentication & Access Control

  • Required Authentication: Bearer JWT token (protect middleware).
  • Role Restriction: Accessible only to customers holding role: 'user' (restrictTo("user")).
  • Email Verification: User account email address must be verified (isEmailVerified: true).

Catalog Validation & Business Rules

  1. Book Existence Verification: Queries MongoDB via Books.findById(bookId). If the target book does not exist in the catalog, the request fails immediately with HTTP 404 Not Found ("Book not exists").
  2. One Review per Customer per Book: The database enforces a compound unique index on { user: 1, book: 1 }. If the authenticated customer has already submitted a review for this book, the creation request is rejected.
  3. Rating Constraints: Rating must be a numerical value between 1 (minimum) and 5 (maximum).

Automated Rating Aggregation Lifecycle

Upon saving a new review, a Mongoose post("save") lifecycle hook triggers:

  • Executes aggregation pipeline Review.calcAvgRating(this.book).
  • Computes the updated cumulative rating count (nRating) and arithmetic average (avgRating).
  • Updates ratingQuantity and ratingAverage fields directly on the corresponding Books catalog document.

Update the authenticated customer's review and rating for a book

Updates the existing review text commentary and/or star rating submitted by the authenticated customer for the designated book.

Authentication & Access Control

  • Required Authentication: Bearer JWT token (protect middleware).
  • Role Restriction: Accessible only to customers holding role: 'user' (restrictTo("user")).
  • Email Verification: User account email address must be verified (isEmailVerified: true).

Operational Logic

  1. Verifies that bookId is supplied in the request path parameters.
  2. Executes Review.findOneAndUpdate({ book: bookId, user: req.user.id }, req.body).
  3. Automated Rating Resynchronization: A Mongoose post(/^findOneAnd/) middleware hook executes immediately after the update:
    • Calls calcAvgRating(doc.book._id) with the reviewed book's ID.
    • Aggregates all current reviews for the book and synchronizes ratingAverage and ratingQuantity on the Books document.

Rate Limiting

  • Protected by mutationLimiter: Maximum 10 mutation requests per minute per client IP.

Operational Logic

Rate Limiting

Retrieve all catalog reviews across all books (Admin only)

Provides comprehensive administrative oversight of all customer reviews submitted across the bookstore catalog.

Authentication & Access Control

  • Required Authentication: Bearer JWT token (protect middleware).
  • Role Restriction: Strictly restricted to users holding role: 'admin' (restrictTo("admin")).
  • Email Verification: Admin account email address must be verified (isEmailVerified: true).

Search & Filtering Capabilities

  • Keyword Search (msg): Optional case-insensitive regular expression substring filter ({ review: { $regex: msg, $options: "i" } }) searched across all review bodies in the database.
  • Catalog-wide Scope: Unlike the book-specific review endpoint, this queries all reviews without filtering by a specific book ID.

Sorting Behavior

  • sort=new (default): Sorts descending by -createdAt (most recently submitted reviews first).
  • sort=old: Sorts ascending by createdAt (oldest reviews first).
  • Any unrecognized or omitted sort option automatically defaults to new.

Pagination Rules

  • page: 1-based page index (defaults to 1).
  • limit: Number of records returned per page (defaults to 10).
  • Upper Bound: If limit exceeds 100, the server automatically caps it at 100.
  • Computes skip = (page - 1) * limit.
  • Computes totalPages = Math.ceil(totalItems / limit) and hasNextPage = page < totalPages.

Data Population

  • Automatically populates the author's public name (user: { _id, name }) and book title (book: { _id, title }) via Mongoose pre(/^find/) query middleware.

Rate Limiting

  • Protected by getRateLimiter: Maximum 30 requests per minute per client IP.

Retrieve current user's review for a book (with Redis caching)

Retrieves the specific review and rating written by the authenticated customer for the designated book, utilizing a high-performance Redis cache-aside caching pattern.

Authentication & Access Control

  • Required Authentication: Bearer JWT token (protect middleware).
  • Role Restriction: Accessible only to customers holding role: 'user' (restrictTo("user")).
  • Email Verification: User account email address must be verified (isEmailVerified: true).
  • Parameter Validation: Middleware validateId("bookId") validates that bookId is a valid 24-character hexadecimal MongoDB ObjectId before controller execution.

High-Performance Redis Cache-Aside Architecture

  1. Cache Lookup: Checks Redis for key user:{userId}:book:{bookId} using client.get(...).
  2. Cache Hit:
    • Returns cached serialized review immediately from Redis memory without querying MongoDB.
    • Responds with HTTP 200 OK: { status: "success", message: "review found successfully", data: JSON.parse(reviewData) }.
  3. Cache Miss:
    • Queries MongoDB for an existing review via Review.findOne({ book: bookId, user: req.user.id }).
    • If no review exists, aborts with HTTP 404 Not Found ("Review not found").
    • If found:
      • Serializes the review document and writes it to Redis key user:{userId}:book:{bookId}.
      • Responds with HTTP 200 OK: { status: "success", data: review }.

Rate Limiting

  • Protected by getRateLimiter: Maximum 30 requests per minute per client IP.

bearerAuth

bookId
required

Example: 683aab454ae6c56e60594eb7

Retrieve all registered users with multi-field search and pagination (Admin only)

Retrieves a paginated list of registered users across the platform for administrative auditing, customer support, and account management.

Authentication & Access Control

  • Required Authentication: Bearer JWT token (protect middleware).
  • Role Restriction: Strictly restricted to users holding role: 'admin' (restrictTo("admin")).
  • Email Verification: Admin account email address must be verified (isEmailVerified: true).

Multi-Field Regex Keyword Search

  • Name Search (name): Case-insensitive regular expression substring match ({ name: { $regex: name, $options: "i" } }).
  • Email Search (email): Case-insensitive regular expression substring match ({ email: { $regex: email, $options: "i" } }).
  • Phone Search (phone): Matches against phone number digits by converting numeric phone to string via MongoDB $expr with $regexMatch.
  • Filters can be combined simultaneously.

Sorting Behavior

  • sort=new (default): Sorts descending by -createdAt (most recently registered accounts first).
  • sort=old: Sorts ascending by createdAt (earliest registered accounts first).
  • Unrecognized or omitted sort parameters default to new.

Pagination Rules

  • page: 1-based page index (defaults to 1).
  • limit: Number of records returned per page (defaults to 10).
  • Upper Bound: If limit exceeds 100, the server automatically caps it at 100.
  • Computes skip = (page - 1) * limit.
  • Computes totalPages = Math.ceil(totalItems / limit) and hasNextPage = page < totalPages.
  • Dynamic response message: "all users found successfully" if records exist, otherwise "users not found".

Active User Query Filter

  • Automatically excludes deactivated accounts ({ isActive: { $ne: false } }) via Mongoose pre(/^find/) hook.

Rate Limiting

  • Protected by getRateLimiter: Maximum 30 requests per minute per client IP.

Add a book to the authenticated user's wishlist

Saves a designated book to the authenticated customer's personal wishlist for future purchase.

Authentication & Access Control

  • Required Authentication: Bearer JWT token (protect middleware).
  • Email Verification: User account email address must be verified (isEmailVerified: true).
  • Parameter Validation: Middleware validateId("bookId") verifies that bookId is a syntactically valid 24-character hexadecimal MongoDB ObjectId.

Verification & Business Rules

  1. Catalog Existence Verification: Queries MongoDB via Books.findById(bookId). If the target book does not exist in the catalog, the request fails immediately with HTTP 404 Not Found ("Book not found").
  2. Duplicate Prevention: Queries Wishlist.findOne({ user: req.user._id, book: bookId }). If the book already resides in the customer's wishlist, the request is rejected with HTTP 400 Bad Request ("Book is already in your wishlist").
  3. Database Uniqueness Constraint: The Wishlist schema enforces a compound unique index { user: 1, book: 1 } guaranteeing concurrency-safe deduplication.

Rate Limiting

  • Protected by mutationLimiter: Maximum 10 mutation requests per minute per client IP.

Remove a book from the authenticated user's wishlist

Removes a designated book from the authenticated customer's wishlist.

Authentication & Access Control

  • Required Authentication: Bearer JWT token (protect middleware).
  • Email Verification: User account email address must be verified (isEmailVerified: true).
  • Parameter Validation: Middleware validateId("bookId") verifies that bookId is a syntactically valid 24-character hexadecimal MongoDB ObjectId.

Operational Logic

  1. Executes Wishlist.findOneAndDelete({ user: req.user._id, book: bookId }).
  2. If no matching wishlist entry is found for this customer and book, the server responds with HTTP 404 Not Found ("Book is not in your wishlist").
  3. Upon successful removal, responds with HTTP 200 OK.

Rate Limiting

  • Protected by generalRateLimiter: Maximum 15 requests per minute per client IP.
